name: What is the difference between a garage conversion and a detached ADU?

mainEntity.name: Which is better for my property: converting the existing garage or building a detached ADU from scratch?
mainEntity.text: Which is better for my property: converting the existing garage or building a detached ADU from scratch?

acceptedAnswer.text: The main difference is whether you are adapting an existing shell or building a new standalone unit. A garage conversion is usually the more efficient option when the structure is sound and the footprint works for the intended floor plan. It can be less disruptive and may save money by preserving foundation, walls, and roof elements. A detached ADU offers greater design flexibility, privacy, and often better long-term value perception, but it usually requires more site preparation, more permitting effort, and more budget. The right choice depends on lot size, garage condition, privacy goals, rental strategy, and how much of the backyard you want to preserve. Homeowners should compare not just construction cost, but also livability, resale appeal, and construction timeline. In many Los Angeles-area properties, conversion is the practical first option unless the existing garage is in poor condition or the owner wants a larger custom unit.
acceptedAnswer.description: A garage conversion uses an existing structure, so it is usually faster and less expensive. A detached ADU starts from new construction, which gives more design freedom, but it usually costs more, takes longer, and may require more site work and utility coordination.
